extracted.intended_audience: U.S. federal policymakers, land-office officials, surveyors, and miners
extracted.subtask_short: public mineral land survey & sale policy
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and procedural standards for surveying, subdividing, appraising, advertising, and selling the United States' public mineral lands (including proposed lot sizes, surveying method, marking, appraisal chain, bidding rules, and disposition of unsold tracts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt the geodetic survey system
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue surveys by townships/sections but adopt the geodetic system for subdividing mineral lands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons given: linear surveys have much greater error (nearly ratio of yards to inches) unacceptable for minute subdivisions (one-acre); geodetic surveys inform interior of tracts, enable Government to appraise every acre, produce proper maps similar to coast survey, and allow people to judge value. Additional cost estimated at hardly two cents an acre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivide gold and silver lands into one-acre tracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The subdivision of the gold and silver lands should be into tracts of one acre each, continuing and extending the present system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from townships of six miles square (36 sections). Convert quarter-quarter (40-acre) subdivisions by successive lines into ten-acre, then five-acre, then five 1-acre tracts. This is presented as the only practicable plan for subdividing sections into one-acre tracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lot dimensions and subdivision pattern for one-acre tracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification of the shape and sizes of the ten-acre, five-acre, and one-acre subdivisions (not square acres).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ten-acre tract exterior east-west lines 110 yards (330 ft) long; north-south sides 44 yards (132 ft). Ten-acre tract subdivided into two 5-acre tracts by a north-south line through the centre; each 5-acre tract subdivided by east-west lines into five 1-acre tracts. Notes that square one-acre subdivisions are impossible and unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking monuments at fixed intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey monuments should mark the subdivision grid on the ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark by stone or iron monuments the north and south exterior lines of each section at intervals of forty-four yards, and the east and west lines at distances of one hundred and ten yards, so the survey extends continuously from section to section and township to township.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue township/section survey framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain the present mode of surveys by townships, sections, and quarter-quarter sections with further subdivisions as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed changes are an extension of the existing system (townships six miles square, 36 sections, 23,040 acres). The geodetic system is to be adopted within that framework to enable minute (one-acre) subdivisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicability limit on minimum claim size
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge practical limits on how small public subdivisions can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many miners' claims are smaller than an acre, but making more minute subdivisions than one acre is impracticable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraisal and valuation chain of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Set roles and workflow for examining, reporting, and fixing values of mineral subdivisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One surveyor, accompanied by one commissioner for each four townships, should examine and report to the register and receiver of the proper land office the value of each subdivision with maps. The register and receiver communicate these views/opinions to the Commissioner of the General Land Office, who, under supervision of the Secretary of the Interior, should fix the value of these acre lots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish appraisals and advertise lands for sale with minimum rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Appraised values should be published and lands advertised for sale at minimum rates not below estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fixed values should be published; lands then advertised for sale to the highest bidder for cash, at minimum rates not below those estimated. Bids should be received after six months' advertisement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized receipt and simultaneous opening of bids
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for receiving and opening bids to ensure fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids, after six months' advertisement, should be received by the register and receiver of the proper land offices, and also by the Secretary of the Interior, up to the same day and hour, when such bids should be at once opened simultaneously, and the land awarded to the highest bidder above the minimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require a 1% bid deposit as security
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent fraud, no bid should be received unless accompanied by a deposit equal to one percent of the bid amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit to be forfeited to the Government only if the bid is successful and the amount is not paid in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of tracts not sold above appraised value
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for handling tracts unsold at or above appraised (minimum) value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such tracts should be disposed of by entry at the minimum price, in the same manner as under the former land system, and remain subject at proper intervals to new appraisements and advertisements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sell other mineral lands in forty-acre lots
rubrics_metrics.description: Non gold-and-silver mineral lands are to be sold in forty-acre lots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subdivision is already recognized by law; the recommendation is to continue selling other mineral lands in forty-acre tracts while gold and silver are sold in one-acre lots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sales and titles to attract capital and develop mines
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy objective: providing certain titles at nominal prices to existing miners and selling new mines at appraised values to attract foreign capital and speed mineral development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument that current lack of titles limits capital; a system of definite titles and fair sales would bring foreign capital, increase investment, and hasten the development of mineral wealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assimilate U.S. gold coinage to British sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to align U.S. gold coinage (retaining decimal system) with British sovereign in gold and alloy content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have in the U.S. half eagle the same amount of gold and alloy as in the British sovereign; stamp equivalency (e.g., 'Equal to a U. S. half eagle' on sovereign and vice versa). This would ease exchange with England, reduce mystery and losses, slightly depreciate present gold coinage but not affect transactions, and promote universal adoption of the decimal system and eventual decimalization/assimilation of weights and measures.
